title: Let screens sleep before you do
description: It is less about the glow than the grip: giving screens a bedtime a little before yours ends the day’s endless scroll.

body.heading: Interesting is the opposite of sleepy
paragraphs: Screens are often blamed for their light, and bright light late at night can indeed push the body clock later. But for most people the bigger effect is simpler: screens are interesting. Arguments, cliffhangers, messages that deserve replies, one more video — all of it keeps the mind in daytime mode, alert and engaged.
Sleep needs the opposite trajectory: stimulation falling, the day closing down. Anything endless and personalised works against that slope, whatever its colour temperature.

body.heading: Give the phone its own bedtime
paragraphs: Choose a time fifteen to thirty minutes before yours when the phone goes to charge — ideally outside the bedroom, or at least across the room — and stays there. Tell the people who matter that you go quiet after that hour; almost nobody minds, and true emergencies have telephones’ oldest feature: the call.
Fill the gap with the analogue end of your wind-down: the book, the shower, the stretches, tomorrow’s clothes. The gap only feels empty for the first few evenings.

body.heading: If a screen must stay, tame it
paragraphs: Sometimes life requires the laptop late: a deadline, a different time zone, a sick relative. Then work with the grain — dim everything, use the warmest display setting, choose finite content over infinite feeds, and keep the last ten minutes for something on paper.
The aim is a trend, not a purity test. Most evenings ending a little earlier and a little calmer will move your sleep more than one perfect digital sunset followed by six ordinary nights.

takeaway: Screens off a little before you are; let the day end on paper, paper-thin and finite.
